unresolved_added: Summary and memo values must be kept distinct from body values.
The repeated red watermark is third-party furniture and must never enter language evidence.
Contents and References are source-order controls, not author argument.
Form fields and page headers are not prose.
The paper has no abstract separate from the Summary sheet.
Missingness thresholds are described but not numerically audited.
Cubic-spline imputation has no residual or sensitivity report.
Fitted-curve replacement has no fit diagnostics.
Averaging other-state data can import cross-state dependence.
All-zero indicators may represent absent technology, not error.
Normalization range and population denominator are not versioned.
Per-capita division may change the interpretation of production and share.
Clean energy includes natural gas and nuclear; this is a substantive definition.
Fuel-category membership is not independently validated.
`U_r`, `U_c` and `GE` mix levels and proportions.
Indicator directions and units are incompletely documented.
Geographic/resource explanations are qualitative.
Population and policy paragraphs do not identify causal effects.
PCA is motivated by correlation but loadings are not fully released.
AHP consistency `CR=.033` is not overall model validation.
Four states and many indicators make weight stability fragile.
Utility function endpoints are imposed rather than estimated.
Median utility `.5` is a subjective anchor.
Piecewise utility sensitivity is not shown.
The ranking is a 2009 cross-sectional claim only.
No confidence interval or rank uncertainty is reported.
ARIMA differencing/order notation is internally ambiguous.
One ACF/PACF exceedance is dismissed as chance without a formal test.
ARIMA residual diagnostics and forecast intervals are incomplete.
California is the detailed example; other-state fit provenance is thin.
State-score forecasts inherit every index and weight assumption.
The no-policy assumption is explicitly unrealistic but required.
Forecast horizons are conditional trajectories, not probabilities.
The 110% uplift has no cost or feasibility derivation.
Pooled four-state renewable-use forecasting changes the unit of analysis.
Aggregation is not a physical electricity-flow model.
Shapley efficiency/symmetry/aggregation/null rules require transferable utility.
Shapley inputs use electricity and price data with unclear units.
Table 9 body total is 343.85 billion.
The memo states a different 208 billion total and different state shares.
This memo/body discrepancy must be preserved as an audit warning.
Market integration names buyers and sellers but omits transmission capacity.
Reliability, storage, congestion and losses are absent.
Prices are treated as sufficient incentives without market-clearing analysis.
Biomass and hydropower are ignored on a saturation assertion.
Tax exemption and subsidy actions have no budget or enforcement path.
State-specific projects are not tied to quantified resource potential.
Demonstration funds lack selection and monitoring criteria.
No equity or burden-sharing analysis accompanies the fund.
No legal authority or implementation timeline is specified.
Strengths are author-reported process claims.
The paper admits only 13 indicators enter the composite score.
Summary variables and body variables need lineage checks.
The utility and ARIMA choices are acknowledged as subjective.
Visual curves and table values must not be copied as generic facts.
Equations are source-specific and should be re-derived, not transplanted.
Original PNGs were never transported to model context.
Every proxy remains under 450,000 bytes and the bundle under 4 MiB.
The paper's page numbering differs between physical pages and printed pages.
A future learner must keep profile, score, forecast, target and recommendation evidence types separate.
